name: Simple Alerts
selection: User-approved replacement research universe: 24 small-AI operating-company research names plus REKR in financing/compliance quarantine. Exactly 25 issuer identities. Selection is qualitative diligence priority, not expected return, a buy recommendation or a validated 10x claim.

requiredLiveGates: AI revenue or paid deployment evidence
research.scenarioPolicy: Extreme long-horizon backsolves are analyst assumptions, not fair values, forecasts, price targets, or alert authority. Numeric research scenarios are not ingested into runtime valuations.

companies.businessEvidence: Services were 85% of revenue; AI-video bookings rose 20% sequentially, with 10 Fortune 500 customers broadening adoption. This is paid fleet software with AI modules, not a pure model vendor.
companies.riskNotes: FY2026 debt was $280m against $40.8m cash/restricted cash; acquisitions and equity compensation can dilute returns.
killCriteria: Services growth fails to accelerate over four quarters
South Africa activation is delayed without replacement demand
Free cash flow after capitalized software remains weak or debt increases

companies.businessEvidence: AI-driven lending network reported $3.5bn quarterly volume and $45m net income attributable to shareholders. Over 35 lender partners provide a real distribution network.
companies.riskNotes: Credit risk retention, financing liabilities and stock dilution require a lender-quality capital model; headline network volume is not revenue.
killCriteria: Credit losses impair retained interests or lender economics
ABS/funding access contracts materially
Net income fails to convert into usable common-share cash

companies.businessEvidence: Reported $69.6M quarterly revenue. Cerence technology was in 50% of worldwide auto production on its TTM company-defined KPI; connected-services revenue grew over 20%. It disclosed a multi-brand Stellantis xUI award and a first Mobile Work Agent customer.
companies.riskNotes: Long automotive design cycles and OEM bargaining power. Q3 includes $12.5M fixed-license revenue; FY2026 Q1 had a $49.5M Samsung IP-license item.
killCriteria: Connected billings or design-win retention stagnate while automakers internalize or replace the stack.
Recurring economics fail to offset declining legacy license revenue.
Cash generation relies on nonrecurring IP/license settlements rather than product demand.

companies.businessEvidence: Reported $92.1M Q2 revenue. Latest results describe paid frontier-lab work, agentic reinforcement-learning programs and proprietary datasets; a Q1 disclosure identified a $1M evaluation-platform engagement. The two largest Q2 customers were 37% and 34% of revenue.
companies.riskNotes: Two customers jointly represented 71% of Q2 revenue. Q2 gross margin and cash include business-model and prepayment nuances requiring normalization.
killCriteria: Loss or meaningful spend reduction by either dominant customer is not replaced promptly.
Synthetic data, automation or customers’ internal teams structurally commoditize its work.
Revenue scales but gross profit, cash generation and revenue per employee deteriorate.

companies.businessEvidence: Q2 originations were $4.2bn and fee revenue $348m; GAAP net income was $16.5m. AI underwriting is the core commercial product.
companies.riskNotes: Loan assets and funding debt matter; convertible notes and employee equity may dilute a per-share outcome.
killCriteria: Vintage credit performance deteriorates versus pricing assumptions
Funding withdrawals force more balance-sheet lending
Secured-product contribution margins fail to improve over four quarters

companies.businessEvidence: FY2026 unmanned-systems revenue was $12.6m with over 30 active engagements. Compute platforms support customers including Swarmer and AVT Australia. Most revenue remains broader IoT.
companies.riskNotes: Reported $60m cash and no debt at June year-end, after capital raising; future acquisitions and equity compensation can dilute.
killCriteria: Unmanned-systems design wins do not convert to revenue over four quarters
Core IoT shrinks faster than AI grows
Acquisitions fail to improve cash generation

companies.businessEvidence: Revenue grew 46%; ACV plus royalties reached $99.5m. Management said most new designs include AI compute; named deployment evidence includes Li Auto and Arm.
companies.riskNotes: Operating losses and stock compensation persist; custom-chip concentration and a premium starting valuation make 10x an unusually high hurdle.
killCriteria: AI design starts do not become production royalties
ACV/RPO growth decelerates for four quarters
Large customers internalize the IP or displace it

companies.businessEvidence: Net sales rose about 90%; Apollo silicon and the helia software stack support on-device AI. SEC reports three end customers at 28.9%, 24.4% and 24.2% of quarterly sales.
companies.riskNotes: June public offering raised about $168m net; recent financing and employee equity show dilution is real, even with a stronger cash buffer.
killCriteria: Growth relies on just the same three customers
New designs fail to broaden the revenue base
Supply constraints or price competition prevent margin expansion

companies.businessEvidence: AI video/sensor management generated $4.12m revenue at 75% gross margin; real sales, but contracts are small and government-driven.
companies.riskNotes: Only $12.37m cash at June 30; warrants, earnouts, customer concentration and microcap liquidity materially raise risk.
killCriteria: Award announcements fail to become collected revenue
Gross margin or recurring mix deteriorates over four quarters
Cash runway drops below 12 months without nondilutive financing

companies.securityDescription: Class A common stock; excludes warrants
companies.businessEvidence: Reported $33.3M Q2 revenue, with $25M space-based intelligence and AI services. The release discloses NRO work, NGA Luno renewals, international subscription conversions and commercial monitoring contracts.
companies.riskNotes: Capital intensive with government concentration and launch/space risks. Common stock is still NYSE listed; the August delisting action applied only to warrants.
killCriteria: Satellite launches or in-orbit performance repeatedly miss commercial requirements.
Government or international contracts fail to renew/convert and backlog stalls.
Constellation replacement costs and share issuance outrun recurring gross-profit growth.
companies.securityNotes: The cited Form 25 concerns warrants, not common shares. Do not infer common-share delisting from a warrant-only filing; confirm the affected security class.

companies.businessEvidence: Ten IP licenses in Q2 included NeuPro-M NPU selection by an unnamed global AI platform company; automotive AI programs contributed royalty growth. Connectivity is still a major business.
companies.riskNotes: Long license-to-royalty lags and equity compensation can dilute returns; AI-only revenue is not separately disclosed.
killCriteria: Major AI licenses do not produce production royalties
Royalty growth stays low despite licensing announcements
R&D and stock compensation outgrow gross profit

companies.businessEvidence: Bristol Myers Squibb agreed to deploy Bunsen AI co-scientist. Q2 ACV was $30m, up 27%; the business combines physics software, AI and drug-discovery economics.
companies.riskNotes: Drug R&D and software investment create financing risk; quarterly profit benefited from investment gains, not recurring operating earnings.
killCriteria: Software ACV fails to sustain growth
AI adoption generates no incremental paid usage
Pipeline or collaboration economics consume rather than return capital

companies.businessEvidence: Reported $61.897M quarterly revenue from conversational AI. Q2 release identifies restaurant expansion with Five Guys, IHOP and Jersey Mike’s, and new Ruby Tuesday agreements. September 30 release documents production voice/generative AI in Kia Sorento.
companies.riskNotes: Loss-making; integration risk; competition from platform vendors. Q2 baseline excludes LivePerson, acquired September 4, 2026.
killCriteria: Organic growth remains below 20% for four quarters while reported growth depends on acquisitions.
Production deployments fail to expand usage or customer ROI; large enterprises substitute bundled incumbent tools.
Cash losses and acquisition/stock-compensation issuance make per-share progress lag enterprise growth.

companies.businessEvidence: Q2 shipped 628,275 lidars, including 142,371 robotics units. Robotics adoption and named AI-device relationships give genuine commercial exposure; prices are falling.
companies.riskNotes: ADS and China-policy risks; one ADS represents eight Class B shares since July 10, 2026. Never multiply ADR price by raw ordinary-share count.
killCriteria: Unit growth is offset by persistent price/margin erosion
Export or procurement restrictions materially block target customers
New initiatives consume cash without durable revenue
companies.securityNotes: One ADS represents eight ordinary shares. Normalize per-ADS prices and ordinary-share counts; do not treat USD convenience translations as the reporting currency.

companies.businessEvidence: Reported $35.1M Q2 revenue, including $13.9M systems integration revenue, up 46%. The business earns fees integrating AI/high-performance computing infrastructure. The 10-Q reports one U.S. IT OEM generated 99% of Q2 revenue.
companies.riskNotes: 99% of quarterly revenue and 100% of June 30 accounts receivable tied to one OEM. Quarterly revenue fell 20% as procurement mix declined; profit mix matters more than headline sales.
killCriteria: The dominant OEM reduces orders, internalizes integration or renegotiates fees downward.
New capacity and $17M readiness investment fail to produce durable gross-profit growth.
Working-capital/factoring or customer concentration absorbs cash and limits returns.

companies.businessEvidence: Quarterly revenue grew 13.2%; company reports more than 50m AI SoCs installed. CV75/CV72 and X7 expand physical/edge inference products.
companies.riskNotes: Cash/investments of $272.3m provide a buffer, but R&D and equity compensation remain substantial; the starting cap already demands large scale.
killCriteria: New accelerator/channel agreements fail to create material revenue
Growth remains low teens while valuation assumes hypergrowth
Competitors win key automotive/industrial designs

companies.businessEvidence: Q2 revenue reached $55m with over 17,000 lidar/camera sensors shipped. Sensing plus perception software serves autonomy applications; not all hardware revenue is AI software.
companies.riskNotes: Hardware scaling, working capital and stock compensation can dilute; current multi-billion cap makes a 10x especially demanding.
killCriteria: Hardware growth slows before cash break-even
Software does not increase recurring economics
Price competition or capex/dilution absorbs the growth

companies.businessEvidence: Reported $52.375M total quarterly revenue, including $49.2M subscription revenue. The release names agreements with Ford, Johnson & Johnson, Holcim, Heidelberg Materials and federal customers. Recognized subscription revenue establishes paid commercial activity.
companies.riskNotes: Turnaround rather than proven sustained growth. Low 32% GAAP gross margin in the latest quarter; persistent loss history.
killCriteria: Revenue continues to contract through the next four quarters despite restructuring.
Pilots and booked agreements do not convert to production subscription revenue.
Stock compensation and cash consumption repeatedly offset revenue growth; hyperscaler tools commoditize the offering.

companies.businessEvidence: Issuer reports 3.31m customers, $1.43bn in-force premium and Q2 claims expense efficiency. AI supports underwriting/service, but returns depend on insurance risk and reinsurance.
companies.riskNotes: Insurance capital requirements and catastrophic loss risk constrain growth; reported revenue changes with reinsurance cessions and is not a clean premium-growth proxy.
killCriteria: Gross loss ratio or reserve development worsens across multiple quarters
Growth depends on uneconomic acquisition costs
Reinsurance/catastrophe exposure impairs capital

companies.businessEvidence: Genentech exercised its first validated neuroscience target option; $7.7m collaboration revenue provides platform evidence, but clinical medicines remain the economic end product.
companies.riskNotes: $556.8m cash/restricted cash at June 30 and stated runway into early 2028; drug development likely needs more capital before commercialization.
killCriteria: Key clinical readouts fail efficacy/safety thresholds
Partners repeatedly terminate or do not advance programs
Cash runway approaches 12 months with weak milestone prospects

companies.businessEvidence: Reported $5.8M Q2 revenue and $24.6M backlog. Evidence directly tied to AI includes a $2.9M Air Force STRATFI option exercise for Palladyne IQ; total program value exceeded $10.6M. Acquired aerospace services also contribute, so total revenue is not pure AI software revenue.
companies.riskNotes: Early commercialization and acquisition-driven growth. $43.7M cash/investments at June 30 versus guided $32M–$36M annual cash burn. Defense award timing and acquisition integration. September 28 Form 25 identifies the removed security class as Warrant; it does not identify common stock.
killCriteria: Demonstrations and development awards do not become recurring production revenue within two years.
Annual cash burn stays near the $32M–$36M 2026 guidance while the revenue base remains small.
Acquisitions/financing dilute holders faster than profitable commercial contracts grow.
companies.securityNotes: The cited Form 25 concerns warrants, not common shares. Do not infer common-share delisting from a warrant-only filing; confirm the affected security class.

companies.businessEvidence: Q2 revenue was $3.238m; over 2,000 robots deployed and hospital-contract extensions provide commercial evidence, but utilization/economics remain early.
companies.riskNotes: Over $240m cash/securities at June quarter-end, but robotics cash burn and acquisitions may consume it rapidly; existing fleet counts are not revenue.
killCriteria: Revenue per robot and utilization fail to improve
Contribution economics remain negative after deployment maturity
Partner concentration or cash burn forces highly dilutive financing

companies.businessEvidence: Q2 revenue was $36.7M; the company attributes growth to Ask Sage GenAI platforms and products. It reported more than 20 new contracts and $269.6M backlog, demonstrating an operating business rather than an AI-name-only issuer.
companies.riskNotes: Government procurement and budget concentration. 13% reported Q2 growth starts from a small base relative to the valuation.
killCriteria: Product and recurring revenue fail to outgrow labor-heavy services.
Backlog fails to convert or major government contracts are lost.
Large acquisitions or equity issuance consume cash without improving revenue and gross profit per share.

companies.businessEvidence: DeepHealth/Digital Health revenue was $32.4m including intersegment sales; ARR reached $105.5m and 63% came from external customers. AI revenue is small relative to imaging operations.
companies.riskNotes: Capital-intensive imaging operations and acquisition debt coexist with AI software; a 10x from $5.5bn is a very high hurdle.
killCriteria: External AI ARR fails to compound
AI product clearance fails to translate to paid deployment
Acquisition debt or reimbursement pressure offsets imaging growth

companies.businessEvidence: Reported $12.7M Q2 revenue and $6.7M recurring revenue. Its AI roadway platforms serve transportation agencies, law enforcement and commercial operators. This is a real operating AI business, but current financial survival is the immediate gate.
companies.riskNotes: 10-Q states substantial doubt about going concern and insufficient existing cash. $15M notes mature Dec 15, 2026 against $9.8M cash at June 30. Nasdaq minimum-bid deadline Oct 26, 2026; common shares remain listed in cited filing.
killCriteria: Cannot refinance or repay the $15M notes due December 15, 2026.
Nasdaq delisting or repeated distressed issuance impairs investability/per-share economics.
Recurring revenue growth fails to deliver sustained operating cash breakeven.
companies.quarantineReason: REKR financing/compliance quarantine: going-concern uncertainty, $15 million notes due 2026-12-15 and Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance deadline 2026-10-26. Ordinary upside and Serious Buy alerts remain blocked; sourced monitoring and downside/risk review remain available. No automatic release on a date or a positive model review.
quarantineReviewRequirements: Primary evidence of financing/debt-maturity resolution and refreshed cash runway
Primary evidence of restored Nasdaq common-share compliance
Explicit reviewed configuration change after current identity, liquidity, dilution and valuation checks
